sections.title: 1 · Which name pairs get confused?
sections.what: 440 real confused pairs from the ISMP list vs 1320 never-reported pairs; 5-fold cross-validation with no name shared between train and test.

sections.title: 2 · Heard-alike: medicine names through speech AI
sections.what: 300 Indian brand names spoken by 2 synthetic voices (600 utterances), transcribed by whisper-large-v3, then looked up.

rows.name: Twinpill learned ranker (trained on one voice, tested on the other)

sections.note: Speech AI spelled only 49% of names exactly right; 7.0% of transcripts were a different real Indian brand.

sections.title: 3 · Does one question separate the twins?
sections.what: For all 6,022 twin names, which single question splits the unrelated medicines.

rows.name: Asked by form (tablet or eye drop?)
Asked by the letters after the name (DSR, Plus…)
Only the company or full printed name tells them apart

sections.note: When only the company differs, Twinpill says so plainly and asks the person to read the company name on the strip.
